release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig Relay converts agentic execution, provider access, protocol calls, bridge events, and generated-code candidates into schema-governed, trace-correlated, content-light, replayable local evidence.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: Cross-surface trace not tested end-to-end. CI evidence and coordination lack trace_id. Providers lack trace_id. Receipt vocabulary is per-surface, not unified.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Per-surface trace and receipt schemas are consistent (all protocol surfaces have trace_id in receipts). SDK receipt_ref is the canonical cross-reference. Cross-surface trace test is proposed as Wave 8 test.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig uses refusal-first capability gates for provider and protocol surfaces.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: MCP refusal envelope is schema-only, never instantiated. ACP refusals are exceptions, not envelopes. Shared refusal vocabulary does not exist.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Bridge, GitHub, Google Workspace, and runtime refusals are strongly proven. MCP and ACP refusal envelopes exist in schema but are not exercised because transports are not yet enabled. Honest gap documented in convergence review.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig treats tool hints/descriptors as untrusted metadata, not authorization.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: MCP tool hints from external servers would be hostile input. Currently not tested because no MCP transport exists.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Rig's tool gate is capability-based, not hint-based. Tool descriptors are metadata, never authorization. MCP tool poisoning research risks are mitigated by refusal-first posture and no live MCP transport.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig records failed compiler candidates and counterexamples as evidence rather than discarding them.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: Compiler is Experiment 0 only. No runtime compiler package exists. Evidence is schema-governed but produced by experiment, not production pipeline.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Compiler v1 is explicitly a contract/feasibility surface. Experiment 0 proves the pipeline works. Full compiler implementation is gated behind feasibility artifact.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig can compare local OTel-derived tool behavior across runs and produce hardening proposals without mutating runtime.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: OTel pipeline is read-side only. Not integrated into live runtime. Data sources are external. No live OTel collector.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: OTel pipeline is a read-side analytical projection. Read-only by design. Hardening proposals are advisory, not runtime enforcement.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig can isolate generated-code candidates in scratch Git worktrees and validate them against a multi-gate matrix.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: Worktree lifecycle is schema-defined and tested in Experiment 0. No production compiler worktree creation. Multi-gate matrix has 10 gate kinds defined.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Experiment 0 exercises the full pipeline in a controlled test. Production compiler implementation is gated. Worktree isolation is Git-native, not a custom sandbox.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig's bridge/backend/frontend channel is schema-governed, trace-correlated, refusal-first, and progressively rendered.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: Browser E2E deferred (CLI constraint). Lifecycle trace rotation deferred. WebSocketStream backpressure represented as bounded queues.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: 34/34 v1 readiness criteria met. All deferred items are documented with mitigations. Static JS tests cover progressive rendering.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig's provider integrations are local-first and content-light in v1.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: Live OAuth deferred. No GitHub App JWT or Google service-account JWT. Credentialed provider mutations refused. Adapters use local fixtures.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Contract-only posture declared. No credentials stored (token_material_stored: false). All live network refused. Local fixtures provide testing surface.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig's agent execution spine is governed by budgets, trace propagation, refusal behavior, and readiness artifacts.
release_paper_claims_supported.required_caveats: Budget constants exist but enforcement is not wired at all levels. cpu/memory/io/network budgets all FALSE in readiness artifact. Cancellation safety not proven.
release_paper_claims_supported.answer_to_attack: Timeout-based tool enforcement and byte caps (bash max bytes, receipt max bytes) provide practical bounds. Full resource budget wiring is v1.1. Cancellation via supervisor timeout is functional.

release_paper_claims_supported.claim_text: Rig's MCP/ACP/A2A/SDK spine is local, refusal-first, and schema-governed in v1.

MCP test gap is an alpha-level honesty issue, not a release claim. Protocol spine is schema-governed contract vocabulary in v1.

rc_recommendation_rationale: The nine v1 surfaces compose into a governed Rig Relay platform. Schemas are consistent (230 validated), trace_id and content_light fields are present in all protocol surfaces, refusal first is proven on bridge/providers/runtime, and 34/34 desktop readiness criteria pass. Two alpha blockers (MCP zero tests and ACP live NotImplementedMethodError stubs) prevent full PROMOTE because they undermine the protocol spine v1 honesty claim. These are not release blockers because no protocol transport exists and no cross-surface behavior is claimed. However, for a release paper, PROMOTE WITH V1.1 HARDENING is the honest recommendation because named cross-surface integration tests and MCP test coverage should land before any public protocol surface claim. The 10 remaining seams are classified: 0 release blockers, 2 alpha blockers (MCP tests, ACP stubs), 8 v1.1 hardening items, and 0 critical resource/safety gaps. No out-of-scope surfaces were touched.
